$comment: Cross-language auth-companion conformance cases (#58) — the SINGLE SOURCE for what every
auth companion must survive: hostile token-endpoint responses, token responses and
store files where companions may differ but must never fail untyped, successful-refresh
fallbacks, hostile store files, and the canonical store records that pin cross-language
store compatibility (the #54 fixture-drift check).
EVERY companion's test suite (Rust, TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, C#) iterates this
file. New hostile cases are added HERE, never to a single language's suite.
Required behavior per table:
- hostile_token_responses: a token-endpoint 2xx with this body must make the
refresh/exchange fail with the language's TYPED auth error (never a raw
KeyError/NullPointerException/panic/untyped throw), and must leave the on-disk
store UNTOUCHED: persisting a blank/expired Bearer would also burn the
still-valid rotated refresh token. A case gives its body as `body` (JSON),
`raw_body` (sent verbatim) or `raw_body_base64` (bytes JSON can't hold). The
malformed shapes, rejected even though the server has already rotated the
refresh token (there is no trustworthy value to persist):
* a body that isn't valid UTF-8 anywhere, unknown fields included (RFC 8259
§8.1: it isn't JSON text at all), or that has anything but whitespace after
the one top-level JSON value;
* a string that isn't valid Unicode (a lone surrogate escape, RFC 8259 §8.2) in
any of the four fields a companion reads: access_token, refresh_token,
token_type, scope. Unknown fields are not validated;
* a non-string access_token, refresh_token or token_type (scope is lenient);
* an expires_in that isn't an integer in 1..=2147483647 (fractional, a numeric
string, beyond the cap, or beyond any machine integer). The cap keeps
`now + expires_in` exact and readable by every companion's store; a
fractional-looking integer such as `3600.0` is implementation-defined.
A case with `must_not_echo` also requires that string (which its body must
contain) to appear NOWHERE in the error's text or in any error it chains (a
cause/inner/wrapped error): parser messages can quote the body, incl. type errors
that name a wrong-typed value, and the body carries token material. The secrets
are 8 characters: some parsers quote only a ~10-character snippet, which must
still contain the whole secret for the check to see the leak.
- implementation_defined_token_responses: 2xx bodies where companions may
legitimately differ (a leading UTF-8 BOM, which RFC 8259 §8.1 lets a parser
ignore; duplicate keys, §4; deep nesting past a parser's depth limit; an
integral float like 3600.0; a key in another case, which Go matches). The
refresh must EITHER succeed and persist access_token = at-refreshed, a
refresh_token that is rt-refreshed or the prior stored one (never empty), and
expires_at = (time of the refresh) + 3600, OR fail with the typed error and
leave the store UNTOUCHED — never an untyped error/panic, never a half-written
store.
- hostile_store_files: loading a store record with this exact file content must
fail with the language's TYPED store-format error — never a zero/null-filled
record that makes is-authenticated lie, and never an untyped crash. A case gives
the file as `content` (text) or `content_base64` (bytes JSON can't hold); a
store file must be valid UTF-8 with no byte-order mark. A case with
`must_not_echo` also requires that string (which its content must contain) to
appear nowhere in the error's text or any error it chains (the store holds
secrets), including type errors that name a wrong-typed value.
- rejected_token_responses: a NON-2xx token-endpoint response. Seed the store and
credentials with `submitted` (so those exact values are what the refresh sends);
the refresh must fail with the typed token-endpoint error carrying `status`, and
leave the store UNTOUCHED. Its body is kept for diagnosis (`must_echo` appears in
the error), but a submitted secret the server echoes back is redacted
(`must_not_echo` appears nowhere in the error or its chain) — EVERY occurrence,
redacted BEFORE the body is cut, so no fragment survives — and the body is capped
at 1024 characters (the cases pin both sides of the cut: a marker ending before
character 1024 is kept, one starting after it is not). No text in the chain
exceeds `max_error_chars` however large the body.
- implementation_defined_store_files: store contents a parser may accept or reject
(nesting past its depth limit). Loading must EITHER return exactly `expected`
OR fail with the typed store-format error — never an untyped crash.
- refresh_success_cases: a SUCCESSFUL refresh (a valid 2xx with this `body`, or
`raw_body` sent verbatim) starting from the stored `prior` record must persist
exactly `expected`: access_token, refresh_token, scope and token_type, and
expires_at = (time of the refresh) + `expected.expires_in`. Fallbacks:
* an omitted, null, empty, whitespace-only (ASCII space/tab and U+00A0; rarer
code points are implementation-defined), or non-string `scope` keeps the prior
grant and the refresh still SUCCEEDS: RFC 6749 §5.1 lets the server omit an
unchanged scope, and `scope` is informational, so failing would burn the
rotated refresh token over it; persisting a blank would erase the grant the
CLI's re-consent check (#116) reads. A real scope string (incl. a valid
surrogate pair) replaces it;
* an omitted, null or EMPTY refresh_token or token_type keeps the prior value
(the server didn't rotate it; persisting "" would make the next refresh
400). On the initial authorization-code exchange there is no prior value, so
an omitted/null/empty refresh_token fails typed there instead.
- valid_records: the canonical on-disk shapes (field names are the wire format
shared by ALL languages — source of truth: oura-toolkit-auth's store.rs). Every
language must load these exact contents, observe these exact field values, and
round-trip them through its own persist path.
